headline: DOTr Reaffirms Suspension of PUV Fare Hikes
deck: The government is keeping public utility vehicle fare increases on hold while fare petitions proceed and interim support measures are extended to drivers and operators.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: Transportation Secretary Giovanni Lopez said fare increases for public utility vehicles will remain suspended amid unstable oil prices and elevated inflation. The Land Transportation Franchising and Regulatory Board will continue hearing pending petitions without immediately implementing an increase.

sections.heading: What we know
paragraphs: Lopez said the administration does not want commuters to carry the added burden. He also warned that higher transport costs could feed into the prices of goods and services while inflation stands at 6.2 percent.
The LTFRB said hearings on fare petitions will resume on Monday and will include experts and commuters. The review may take several weeks.

sections.heading: Background and context
paragraphs: Public utility vehicle fares are reviewed through LTFRB petitions and hearings rather than changed by announcement alone. The current review must weigh commuter affordability against the fuel and operating costs faced by drivers and operators while inflation remains elevated.

sections.heading: Interim support
paragraphs: The fuel subsidy was raised from ₱10 to ₱12 per liter. The terminal-fee waiver for PUVs at the Parañaque Integrated Terminal Exchange was extended through the end of the year, toll discounts or exemptions for provincial buses were set to begin on August 10, and monthly terminal fees at 86 SM transport terminals were waived beginning August 15.

sections.heading: What remains unclear
paragraphs: The final outcome and timetable of the fare petitions remain unsettled. Detailed eligibility and implementation rules for each support measure should be confirmed through official transport-agency announcements.

sections.heading: Why this matters
paragraphs: A continued fare freeze protects daily household budgets in the short term, especially for workers and students who rely on multiple rides. Drivers and operators, however, continue to face fuel and operating-cost pressure while the petitions are reviewed.

sections.heading: What happens next
paragraphs: The LTFRB will resume public hearings and consult commuters, experts, and transport groups before completing its review. Existing fare increases remain suspended unless the government announces a change.
